A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Corrective Frank-Wolfe research. All 31 pages of v1 and 40 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, algorithms, figures, and tables, support comparison. Some experimental descriptions conflict internally, but the material is complete and readable.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E report original computational experiments on regression, entanglement detection, projection, SOCGS, and tensor completion.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix F report original computational experiments, including revised benchmark comparisons and a new 37-instance analysis.

M1.justification: V3 adds an infeasible-system fallback to QC-MNP and introduces an LP-based variant that selects among nonunique affine minimizers by maximizing the feasible update (Appendix C.1, Algorithm 8). This changes the correction procedure and is required by its finite-termination proof. V3 also removes global pairwise steps from the general corrective-step proposition.

E1.justification: The task families and gisette dataset remain. Entanglement input conditions change: v1 explicitly uses noise parameter v=0.946 in Section 4.2, whereas v3 presents the base Horodecki states there and reports v=0.95,0.97 in Appendix F.2. The exact second appendix noise level remains uncertain because Figure 6 still lists v=1.0.

E2.justification: Figures 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, and 10 add FW, AFW, and PFW to the retained comparisons; tensor completion also retains BCG. The SCG and ALM comparisons add vanilla FW, and SOCGS adds AFW for inner steps. Appendix F.6 additionally compares four base algorithms with eight quadratic-correction hybrids.

E3.justification: Appendix F.6 introduces a 37-instance protocol with explicit time limits, iteration limits, and optimality thresholds. Birkhoff projection changes its n=300 budget from 30 to 60 minutes, and Figure 10 revises tensor-instance configurations. Figure 4 changes inner budgets from k=100,200 to k=50,200 and displays longer runs, although Appendix F.4 retains the earlier settings.

E4.justification: New Appendix F.6 tests whether corrections help FW, AFW, and PFW beyond BPCG and measures how often corrections are fully corrective across four problem families. Figure 11 and Tables 1–2 provide new comparative and mechanism analyses. The existing sparsity, noise, intersection, step-schedule, and PVM line-search analyses are largely retained or revised.

E5.justification: Appendix F.6 newly mentions varying seeds and reports shifted geometric means of successful and total correction counts. This adds aggregation and seed information, without establishing an increase in repeated runs. Neither version provides confidence intervals, significance tests, or a fixed repetition count.

E6.justification: Most benchmark figures contain revised trajectories and additional comparator results. The Birkhoff-projection report changes from a QC runtime advantage to worse runtime under the revised comparisons. New Tables 1–2 report, for entanglement detection, successful/total correction geometric means of 2/473 for BPCG-LP and 596/889 for BPCG-MNP. Changed settings preclude treating these revisions as uniform same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: V3 adds strict-complementarity assumptions, finite face identification, affine-minimizer propositions, and finite-termination results with proofs. It formally extends the sharpness-dependent convergence bounds and derives the new QC-MNP LP. The SCG proof also corrects an inequality direction and its final denominator. The SOCGS theorem newly summarized in the main text largely retains v1's appendix result.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions now claim finite optimal-face identification and finite convergence of quadratic corrections under suitable conditions. Framework examples shift from including PFW to explicitly including BCG. The existing SCG acceleration and generalized-self-concordant SOCGS claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 substantially qualifies the acceleration narrative: Birkhoff projection exposes correction overhead and a need to tune correction frequency, while longer SOCGS inner runs reduce the advantage and can match AFW. It also explains missing/nonunique affine minimizers and uses correction-success statistics to discuss why QC-LP helps unevenly across methods and problems.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly states that all compared methods use secant line search and identifies the expanded baselines as lazified. Appendix F.6 supplies stopping thresholds and budgets for its new comparison. Hardware, FrankWolfe.jl usage, caching guidance, and most existing implementation details remain; the broader line-search statement alone does not establish a changed implementation.

R1.justification: V3 adds Bomze et al. on active-set identification and Vinyes–Obozinski on column generation, while removing the Besançon–Kurtz, Mazanti et al., and Oustry–Cerulli references. It gives existing BCG work a more explicit foundational role. Publication updates and the repaired Horodecki citation do not introduce additional works.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites affect the abstract, contributions, corrective-step explanations, and experimental discussion, with notation and language editing throughout. Acknowledgments move before the references, and Sébastien Designolle joins the author list. The main section sequence remains stable; much appendix expansion consists of new scientific content.

P2.justification: V3 adds Figure 11 and Tables 1–2 and redraws most benchmark plots with expanded legends and comparator curves. Entanglement plots adopt logarithmic horizontal axes, Figure 5 rearranges metric rows, and Figure 10 reorganizes its instance panels. Local pairwise and fully-corrective steps also receive separate algorithm displays.

improvement.justification: Broader baselines, explicit handling of missing/nonunique affine minimizers, and more qualified runtime conclusions make v3 more useful than v1. The net gain is limited by conflicting Figure 4/F.4 and Figure 6/F.2 settings, F.6 counting budget exhaustion as 'solved,' and Proposition 5 incorrectly equating span(S) with the span of differences v−w. These issues weaken reproducibility and parts of the added evidence.
